name: The Everyday Go-To
why: Both cool, clear tones — same palette track.

name: Neutral Reset
why: White + seafoam reads clean, no clash risk.

name: Statement Bottom
why: Salmon carries the outfit — keep the top neutral.

name: Clean Base, Earth Bottom
why: Corrected: the heavyweight tee is Relaxed Fit (verified against Zara's own listing), same volume class as the jogger — two loose pieces together reads sloppy at 172cm. jj-tee-white's regular fit is the only owned casual top that can balance relaxed loungewear correctly.

name: Utility Contrast
why: Corrected: previously paired a Relaxed-fit tee with baggy cargo — both loose, the exact combo the cargo's own note warns against. White regular-fit top now carries the contrast instead of a tonal grey-to-black match.

name: Activate the Woodland
why: Corrected: swapped the relaxed jogger for the regular-fit khaki denim so the relaxed tee has a fitted counterpoint — still rugged-casual, still finally gives the boot an outfit, and gives the previously-unpaired khaki denim its first look too.

name: Forest, Earth Base
why: Replaces the old 'Purple + Black' pairing, which relied on a Relaxed tee + baggy cargo combo that no longer passes proportion rules. Dark green (relaxed) needs a fitted/regular bottom, not another loose one — khaki denim fits and was otherwise sitting with zero outfits of its own.

name: The One Smart Option (today)
why: As close to business-casual as the current wardrobe gets.

name: Statement Shirt, Plain Base
why: The one patterned piece already owned — its own note says pair with plain neutral bottoms only, since the stripe is already doing the work. Gives it its first complete look.

name: Client Day
why: 60/30/10 — navy, white, tan/steel accent.

name: Daily Elevated
why: Your one validated jewel tone, near the face.

name: AC-Swing Fix
why: Tonal navy column + decoupled indoor layer.

name: Sky Blue Basics
why: Classic office pairing, no jacket needed.

name: Charcoal Everything
why: Single neutral, zero clash risk.

name: Weekend Denim
why: Dark denim reads fine with tan or black belt.

name: Stone Bridge
why: Bridges old earth-tone habits with the new palette.

name: Wine Layer, Cool Evening
why: Second validated jewel tone, warmer register.

name: Flight Day
why: Corrected, two fixes: the overshirt is relaxed and so, now correctly, is the heavyweight tee — stacking two loose pieces reads sloppy, so the regular-fit jj-tee-white goes underneath instead. Also swapped chino-navy for jeans-dark, since business-casual chino paired with an athletic sneaker was too wide a formality gap to read as deliberate.

name: Monsoon Commute
why: Corrected: the original business shirt + chino + athletic sneaker combo was too wide a formality gap (and impractical — leather dress shoes don't belong in monsoon rain anyway). Elevated-casual polo + dark jeans is the realistic register for a rainy commute in sneakers, shell over the top for the AC/rain swing.

name: Abroad, Off-Duty
why: Low-maintenance, no ironing needed on the road.

name: Festive Register
why: Separate formality register — not Western business-casual at all.

name: Navy Shirt, Seafoam Base
why: The 30-day navy MTM shirt had zero outfits built around it — same neutral-plus-cool-pastel formula as the everyday tee look, just in the business-casual register.

name: First Pattern, Kept Low-Risk
why: The houndstooth stays subtle because everything below it is solid navy and tan — deliberately restrained per the roadmap's own reasoning for adding this shirt.

name: Second Register, Work
why: The angular frame gives work days a second visual register, distinct from the Zweig's rounded everyday softness.

name: Gym Session
why: The only fully athletic-register look in the wardrobe — pre-empting the incoming gym habit.

name: Abroad, Off-Duty (Sun)
why: Same low-maintenance travel base as the Zweig version, swapped for sunglasses when it's actually sunny out.

name: Olive on Khaki
why: Restores the olive tee's outfit after the Relaxed-fit correction moved it off the (also relaxed) cream jogger — tonal earth column, now with a regular-fit bottom instead of a second loose piece.
